# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

- Iteration 1 (cand_0001): with an empty seed, reusing a sibling run's champion (same benchmark, same val split) as the base was far cheaper than writing from scratch. Its FINAL traces doubled as a free diagnosis set: this run's trajectories held only scores. Lesson: when the trajectories lack transcripts, look for sibling-run traces before spawning fresh analysis. The sibling's rejected list showed that every add-on to its champion regressed, so this iteration kept additions under ~400 words and scoped each to explicit instruction words or skeleton code. Prose-only rules were kept to a minimum.

## Iteration 2 (cand_0002)
- Strategy tried: diagnose every failing trace against golden, then fix with EVIDENCE-SURFACING levers (skeleton prints, a full-range verify scan, a mapping-comment contract) instead of more prose rules. Rationale: 9 of 13 failures had the deciding evidence in the workbook, but the agent's own prints never showed it (partial row samples, an unprinted desired sheet, a verify step that covered only the written cells). Result pending.
- Signal worth noting: iter1's "broke" set (188-39, 45896, 48975, 51680, 547-43) was not caused by its §2 word list, judging from the traces. They are inspection failures that the sibling champion passed by chance. The LEDGER "broke" set measures change relative to the sibling base, not necessarily causation.
- The feedback text can mislead the diagnosis. 183-8's feedback said "FORMULAS", but the real cause was an untouched '#DIV/0!' totals row. The "int where bool" messages come from the scorer's bool→float transform. Always open the golden before trusting the class in the feedback.
- What to try next: if this iteration accepts, the remaining cracks are 45944 (comparison direction) and 51680 (golden rewrites the examples). Both are probably not worth an iteration. Instead, check flakiness on the passing set.
